newsitem.title: USA: FCC opens NextWave to greater foreign ownerhsip.
newsitem.headline: FCC opens NextWave to greater foreign ownerhsip.

text.p: Privately-held NextWave Telecom Inc said on Monday that the Federal Communications Commission granted its request to exceed applicable foreign-ownership limitations in light of expected new regulations by the World Trade Organization.
The company said that the decision gives its access to world captial markets and it expects to "pursue in the immediate future" all the options that the FCC action now allows.

NextWave is building an all-digital nationwide PCS network to provide airtime to other carriers and resellers on a wholesale basis. The company, which is planning a public offering, has licenses covering 150 million potential customers, for which it has spent $4.7 billion.

In a separate news development, the company said that it has entered into a memorandum of understanding with the National Wireless Resellers Association to promote personal communications service (PCS) resale opportunities.
Under the plan, NWRA members would be eligible to purchase PCS minutes at a flat rate, and with certain other charges eliminated.
